profile.name: Karthik Chandrasekaran
profile.tagline: Building high-performing teams and trustworthy enterprise AI platforms.
profile.summary: I lead engineering teams at Microsoft, connecting enterprise AI, information retrieval, cloud architecture, and security. My work combines technical strategy and hands-on engineering to make quality, cost, and trust explicit design decisions.

focusAreas.title: Engineering leadership
focusAreas.description: Creating clarity, growing leaders, and building teams that can deliver ambitious outcomes sustainably.

focusAreas.title: AI & information retrieval
focusAreas.description: Connecting retrieval quality, permission-aware grounding, agent evaluation, and cost-aware architecture to dependable AI experiences.

focusAreas.title: Cloud architecture
focusAreas.description: Designing distributed systems, microservices, and cloud platforms with reliability and operability in mind.

publications.title: The Governance Layer Nobody Regulates
publications.description: An editorially reviewed essay on why enterprise AI governance must protect information at retrieval time through authorization, provenance, and defense in depth. Scheduled for November 17; a public article link will be added after release.

publications.title: We’re Just Scratching the Surface of What AI Agents Can Do for Service Reliability
publications.description: Why modern systems excel at detecting problems quickly but still struggle to make immediate action safe, and how AI agents can help close that gap.

publications.title: The Moving Target: Why Evaluating RAG Is AI’s Quietest Hard Problem
publications.description: Why evaluation—not retrieval—is the real bottleneck in production RAG, and why trustworthy systems need continuous measurement across retrieval quality, generation quality, cost, and drift.

publications.title: What Conflict Resolution Taught Me About Building AI
publications.description: An engineering leader’s perspective on disagreement as useful information, psychological safety, power dynamics, missing context, and a practical diagnose–prepare–engage–repair framework.

publications.title: Bridging Retrieval Performance and Learning Outcomes: An Integrated Offline and Online Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented AI in Higher Education
publications.description: Co-authored with Gothai Sundaram, this preprint proposes an integrated framework connecting offline retrieval metrics with staged, online evidence of student learning outcomes.

publications.title: LLM Evaluation Is a Manufacturing Quality Problem. We’re Treating It Like a Software Unit Test
publications.description: A manufacturing-quality approach to enterprise RAG evaluation using offline golden datasets, online telemetry, and continuous measurement of context precision, faithfulness, and answer relevance.

publications.title: Evaluating Retrieval and Search Systems for Real-Time Mortgage Underwriting
publications.description: A framework combining offline and online evaluation for retrieval systems in high-stakes workflows.

research.title: Code Mode for Token-Efficient Agentic Access to Large Enterprise Knowledge Stores: A Study on Inventory Management and Product Catalogs
research.description: Studied how a compact typed API and sandboxed computation can keep intermediate records outside an agent's context window. A token-cost model and five synthetic workloads quantify the tradeoffs against direct tool calling; these are controlled benchmark results, not production savings.

research.title: Bloom-Filter Cost Savings for RAG–LLM Evaluation in Offline Validation
research.description: Designed a cost-aware evaluation approach combining Bloom filters, cached verdicts, and optional verification before reuse. A controlled QA proxy benchmark reported 61.2% lower modeled evaluation cost with 99.2% label agreement using a deterministic reference judge, not a production LLM deployment.

research.title: DTM Grounding Allocation: Value-Weighted Token Budgeting for Enterprise Retrieval-Augmented Generation
research.description: Proposed a training-free policy for distributing a fixed grounding-token budget across retrieved evidence using relevance estimates and length-capped weighted allocation. Evaluated retained answer words on SQuAD and HotpotQA; the measurements do not establish generated-answer accuracy or production token savings.

research.title: SovereignRAG-Eval: Compute- and Sovereignty-Aware Offline-to-Online Retrieval Evaluation
research.organization: Africa in AI Workshop at NeurIPS 2026
research.description: Proposed an evaluation protocol joining human relevance judgments, locally validated model judges, consented online comparisons, and query-level resource accounting. Addresses multilingual quality, compute constraints, and data sovereignty. This is protocol research accepted to the workshop, not the NeurIPS main conference; no deployment gains are claimed.

research.title: Benchmark-Driven Login Risk Assessment under LLM-Driven Agentic Browsing
research.description: Developed a threat model and evaluation framework combining fingerprint, behavioral, contextual, and drift signals for adaptive authentication. Validation uses a tabular fraud-data proxy and synthetic adversarial scenarios, not real browser-agent traffic. Presentation and proceedings publication remain pending.

talks.title: Enterprise AI Governance and Secure Grounding: Privacy, Zero Trust, and Observability in Agentic AI Systems
talks.description: Translated enterprise AI architecture into practical R/Shiny workflows: permission-aware retrieval, task contracts, privacy-safe observability, calibrated evaluation, and risk-based release decisions. Presented in a personal capacity.

talks.title: Beyond Accuracy: Engineering Evals for Trustworthy Agentic AI
talks.description: Shared an engineering approach to evaluating agent behavior beyond answer accuracy, including task success, authorization boundaries, failure recovery, reliability, latency, and cost. Speaker and session are listed in the official conference archive; participation was in a personal capacity.

projects.title: Encrypted Patient-Record Provenance
projects.description: Built an encrypted FHIR provenance proof of concept for Public Invention's Global Patient Record Project, with signed record histories and a provider-neutral storage interface. A synthetic-data demonstrator, not a clinically deployed health-record system.
